1376 instance types priced
+20.6% median Seoul premium over N. Virginia, across the 766 types both price
-4.8% median Seoul premium over Tokyo, across the 769 types both price
62% median 3-year reserved saving in Seoul, over the 582 types AWS offers a reservation for
70% median spot saving in Seoul, over the 691 of 774 types the advisor covers
-10.3% Graviton against x86 in Seoul, median over 43 matching shapes
602 types priced elsewhere but not in Seoul

Linux, shared tenancy, list price. No licence, no pre-installed software, no capacity reservation, no Savings Plan. The region columns are on-demand and carry no commitment; the RI and Spot columns are what a commitment or an interruptible instance buys.

The RI columns are the cheapest standard reserved price for that term, as an effective hourly rate: the upfront amount divided by the term (8760 and 26280 hours) plus the recurring rate. The payment option is not assumed — all three are priced and the cheapest wins — and whatever it costs up front is shown beside the rate, because a rate conditional on cash today is not comparable to one that is not. convertible reservations are excluded: they cost more and buy the right to change instance family later, which is a different purchase rather than a dearer one.

The Spot column is an estimate, not a quote: AWS publishes a whole-percent saving over a trailing window, and this applies it to the on-demand price in the same row. The figure beside it is how often spot reclaims that instance in a given hour — a deep saving at >20% is a different product from a shallower one at <5%, so the two are always shown together. Types the advisor does not cover show no spot figure rather than a zero.

Prices come from the AWS Price List Bulk API, fetched once a day and baked into this page at build time — nothing is requested while you read it. Price book 20260806171752. These are list prices for Linux on shared tenancy: Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot, Enterprise Discount Programs and any licence you bring all move the real number. Check the AWS Pricing Calculator before committing to anything. Monthly figures are the hourly price times 730 hours, the convention AWS's own calculator uses. Spot savings and interruption frequencies come from the Spot Instance Advisor, which is the only spot source that needs no AWS credentials — there is no public spot price feed, so the Spot column is derived rather than quoted. Azure and GCP are not here yet — neither publishes vCPU and memory beside the price without either an API key or a specs table written by hand, and a hand-written one is wrong in ways nothing surfaces.
